USMLE-style practice · Pediatrics

Gastroschisis: 2

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A newborn with uncovered bowel outside the abdomen needs careful thermal protection and fluid management. Which physiological consequence of exposed viscera explains these needs beyond the structural problem of the abdominal-wall defect itself?

  1. Gastroschisis
  2. Assess associated structural and chromosomal abnormalities
  3. Protect exposed or vulnerable viscera and prevent heat and fluid loss
  4. Increased heat and fluid loss from exposed bowel
  5. Omphalocele
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Increased heat and fluid loss from exposed bowel

Uncovered bowel in gastroschisis increases fluid and thermal management needs.

Understanding the options

Increased heat and fluid loss from exposed bowel
Uncovered bowel in gastroschisis increases fluid and thermal management needs.
Omphalocele
A midline umbilical defect with herniated organs covered by a membrane suggests omphalocele. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Gastroschisis
Usually right paraumbilical uncovered bowel protrusion suggests gastroschisis. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Assess associated structural and chromosomal abnormalities
Omphalocele is associated with other anomalies, requiring coordinated evaluation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Protect exposed or vulnerable viscera and prevent heat and fluid loss
Neonatal abdominal-wall defects require prompt stabilization and specialist surgical care. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
